title: The determinant weight does not depend on the coefficient field
statement:
Let $X_0$ be a normal geometrically connected curve over $k_0$, fix
$\iota:\Qlb\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf C$, and let $\mathcal V$ be an
irreducible lisse Weil sheaf of rank $r$ on $X_0$ whose
representation is defined over finite extensions
$E\subseteq E'$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$. If
$\hyperref[def-mg-determinant-line]{\det(\mathcal V)}$, read with
coefficients in $E$, is
punctually $\iota$-pure of weight
$a$, then it is punctually $\iota$-pure of the same weight $a$ when
read with coefficients in $E'$.

proof.text: Choose the given $E$-model $V_E$ of the Weil representation and an $E$-basis $e_1,\ldots,e_r$. Reading it over $E'$ means $V_{E'}=E'\otimes_E V_E$, with $g(b\otimes v)=b\otimes\rho_E(g)v$. The coordinate maps $b\otimes\sum_i c_i e_i\mapsto (bc_i)_i$ and $(b_i)_i\mapsto\sum_i b_i\otimes e_i$ are inverse, so $1\otimes e_i$ is an $E'$-basis. For a closed point $y$, use its local geometric Frobenius element as in [sk-d-real-weil]. If $A_y$ is its matrix over $E$ and $j:E\hookrightarrow E'$ is the inclusion, then $F_y(1\otimes e_j)=\sum_i j((A_y)_{ij})(1\otimes e_i)$; hence its matrix over $E'$ is the entrywise image $j(A_y)$.

source.place: Proof: scalar extension of the Frobenius matrices and the punctual-purity equality

proof.text: The permutation formula gives $\det(j(A_y))=\sum_{\sigma\in S_r}\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma)\prod_i j((A_y)_{i,\sigma(i)})=j(\sum_{\sigma\in S_r}\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma)\prod_i(A_y)_{i,\sigma(i)})=j(\det A_y)$, since the inclusion preserves finite sums, products and integer signs. This is a direct finite calculation, with no separability or diagonalizability assumption.

source.place: Proof: scalar extension of the Frobenius matrices and the punctual-purity equality

proof.text: By [def-mg-determinant-line], the local Frobenius on the determinant line is multiplication by $d_y=\det A_y$ over $E$, and by $j(d_y)$ over $E'$. Each line has precisely that scalar as its eigenvalue in $\Qlb$: if a nonzero vector $v$ satisfies $dv=\alpha v$, then $(d-\alpha)v=0$ forces $d=\alpha$. The fixed inclusions $E\subseteq E'\subseteq\Qlb$ send $d_y$ and $j(d_y)$ to the very same element $\alpha_y$ of $\Qlb$. Thus the two determinant lines have the same local eigenvalue at every $y$.

source.place: Proof: scalar extension of the Frobenius matrices and the punctual-purity equality

proof.text: The hypothesis and [def-weil-punctual-weights] give $|\iota(\alpha_y)|=q_y^{a/2}$ for each closed point $y$, where $q_y=\#\kappa(y)$. The preceding step identifies the $E'$-coefficient determinant eigenvalue with this same $\alpha_y$ in the fixed algebraic closure. Neither $q_y$, the fixed map $\iota$, nor $a$ changes. Therefore the identical equality holds at every closed point for the $E'$-coefficient determinant line; the definition says exactly that it is punctually $\iota$-pure of weight $a$.

lean.statement: theorem isPunctuallyPure_det_coefficientExtension {K : Type u} [Field K] [Finite K] {X : Scheme.{u}} {p : X ⟶ Spec (.of K)} [IsConnectedCurve p] (_hNormal : IsNormalScheme X) (W : WeilGroup p) (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (_hl : l ≠ ringChar K) (iota : PadicAlgCl l ≃+* ℂ) (E E' : IntermediateField (Padic l) (PadicAlgCl l)) [FiniteDimensional (Padic l) E] [FiniteDimensional (Padic l) E'] (hEE' : E ≤ E') {r : ℕ} (ρ : W.carrier →* Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup (Fin r) E) (_hIrreducible : Representation.IsIrreducible ((Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.toRepresentation (Fin r) (PadicAlgCl l)).comp ((Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.map E.subtype).comp ρ))) (_hLisse : ∀ i j : Fin r, Continuous fun g : W.geometric ↦ E.subtype (ρ g.val i j)) (a : ℝ) (hPure : ∀ x : X.finitePoints, ‖iota (E.subtype ((W.representedDegreeDatumOfMatrix ρ).det.rep (W.frobenius x) 0 0))‖ = (X.pointNorm x.val : ℝ) ^ (a / 2)) : ∀ x : X.finitePoints, ‖iota (E'.subtype ((W.representedDegreeDatumOfMatrix ((Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.map (IntermediateField.inclusion hEE').toRingHom).comp ρ)).det.rep (W.frobenius x) 0 0))‖ = (X.pointNorm x.val : ℝ) ^ (a / 2)
lean.note: A basis of the given finite coefficient model identifies scalar extension with entrywise mapping of its GL matrices. Uses the recorded RepresentedDegreeDatum.det, actual finite subfields of the fixed PadicAlgCl, and the literal punctual-purity norm equality specialized to its unique rank-one Frobenius eigenvalue. The auxiliary definition only packages the existing Weil degree datum with the given representation.
